q: Which production forms are allowed in Chomsky normal form (apart from S → ε)?
options: A → aα, with α a string of variables
A → α, for any string α
explain: CNF allows exactly two variables, or exactly one terminal, on the right side. A → aα is Greibach normal form.

q: In Greibach normal form, every production has the form…
options: A → aα, where α is a (possibly empty) string of variables
explain: Each production starts with exactly one terminal, followed only by variables.

q: A grammar is in CNF. How many derivation steps does it take to derive a string of length n ≥ 1?
explain: It takes n − 1 steps of the form A → BC to create n variables, then n steps of the form A → a to turn them into terminals.

q: A grammar is in GNF. How many derivation steps does it take to derive a string of length n?
explain: Each GNF step produces exactly one terminal, so n terminals need exactly n steps.

q: The grammar S → aSb | ab is in Chomsky normal form.
explain: False. Both right sides mix terminals or have more than two symbols. CNF needs A → BC or A → a.

q: Which grammar is a correct CNF version of S → aSb | ab?
options: S → XT | XY, T → SY, X → a, Y → b
S → XSY | XY, X → a, Y → b
S → aSb | XY, X → a, Y → b
explain: Terminals are replaced by X → a and Y → b, and the three-symbol rule XSY is split using T → SY. Every rule then has the form A → BC or A → a.

q: Left recursion (A → Aα) must be removed when converting a grammar to Greibach normal form.
explain: True. A left-recursive rule starts with a variable, and keeps doing so however far you expand it. Rewrite A → Aα | β as A → β | βA′ and A′ → α | αA′.

q: Which grammar is in Greibach normal form?
options: S → AB, A → a, B → b
explain: Each rule of the first grammar is a terminal followed only by variables. aSb ends with a terminal, SA starts with a variable, and AB has no leading terminal.

q: Which parsing algorithm needs its grammar in Chomsky normal form?
explain: CYK fills a table of substrings, combining two smaller parts at each step. That relies on every rule being A → BC or A → a.

q: In a CNF parse tree of a string of length n ≥ 1, how many internal nodes use a rule of the form A → BC?
explain: A binary tree with n leaf-parents (one for each A → a) has n − 1 binary branching nodes.
